subject: Post-demo: Data fencing preference and ops clauses
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@wellpath-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Data fencing preference and ops clauses

Hi Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a clear pilot: 

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Primary objective: allow clinical staff to run patient-matching and summarization without PHI leaving WellPath's controlled environment.
- Preferred operational model: looking at Dedicated capacity for predictable latency but leadership wants Private VPC or on-prem options if data control requirements escalate.
- Security asks from the call: keystore residency (BYOK), audit log retention 7 years, and network egress restrictions for model telemetry.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm?):
1) Which datasets must never traverse Redwood's hosted control plane? (e.g., full patient identifiers vs. hashed keys)
2) Is BYOK mandatory for the pilot or acceptable as a canary step after an initial Dedicated deployment?
3) Do you have a preferred keystore vendor (e.g., AWS KMS vs. on-prem HSM) — I can align ops with that.

Our immediate ask: if you can share a one-page network diagram and the security mailbox (security@wellpath-health.com) contact, we’ll validate the Private VPC handshake requirements and timeline.

I attached a short draft SLA we discussed as a starting point for procurement.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm answers to the three clarifying questions above by EOD Wednesday.
- If comfortable, schedule a 45-min alignment call with your security ops and ours (Ben + Karthik) next week to walk the network and keystore specifics.

Thanks —
Mina

Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: WellPath-SLA-draft.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@wellpath-health.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, security@wellpath-health.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data fencing preference and ops clauses

Hi Mina —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers inline below and a few notes from our security lead.

1) Datasets that must never leave our VPC: full MRNs, SSNs, and unredacted patient identifiers. Derived tokens/hashes used for matching are OK to move if reversible mapping keys remain in our custody.
2) BYOK is preferred for production; for the pilot, our Security team can accept Redwood-managed keys if we have an auditable migration plan and a signed SLA.
3) Preferred keystore: AWS KMS with an option to rotate to our on-prem HSM in later phases.

Security note (from security@wellpath-health.com): audit log retention of 7 years is a hard requirement for regulated data; we also want traffic to be restricted to specific egress IPs and for token-level telemetry to be scrubbed of identifiers. There is a short internal network diagram attached.

We'll attach a sanitized network drawing and a one-page control list by tomorrow morning. In terms of deployment preference: leadership leans Dedicated for speed-to-value, but Security will require a Private VPC for any workload that processes full identifiers.

Happy to onboard via a 45-min meeting next Tues/ Wed — propose Wed 10am PT.

Best,
Rajiv
Chief Product Officer, WellPath Health
rajiv.m@wellpath-health.com | +1 (617) 555-6280

Attachments: wellpath-network-drawing.png (PNG, redacted)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data fencing preference and ops clauses

Folks —

Thanks for the notes. A few operational observations and options to present on the call with WellPath: 

- Dedicated capacity is our fastest path: predictable latency, reserved GPU pools, and we can implement strict egress ACLs and token-scrubbing before telemetry leaves their environment. However, any flow that touches full identifiers would require either (a) Private VPC deployment or (b) an on-prem connector that keeps identifiers resident.
- BYOK flows: we can support AWS KMS right away. Migration to an on-prem HSM (via PKCS#11 bridge) is feasible but will add ~4-6 weeks for ops and testing.
- Audit logs: we can provide compressed export hooks to their S3 with encryption-in-transit and sign-off on retention policies; long-term retention (7 years) is fine but will require a storage add-on in the contract.

Ask for the alignment call: I recommend we (Ben + Karthik + Mina) review their network diagram and the sanitized list of assets before Wed so we can produce a concise checklist for the security call. If they want Private VPC in pilot, we should surface the lead time and additional cost expectation up-front.

I've drafted a short ops checklist we can share in the prep email — will attach a link in the HubSpot note.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-3400
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@wellpath-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, security@wellpath-health.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data fencing preference and ops clauses

Rajiv —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the redacted network diagram. Next steps to keep momentum: 

1) Proposed pilot scope: start on Dedicated capacity with pseudonymized payloads only (matching keys retained by WellPath) so we can validate latency and integration within 2–3 weeks.
2) Parallel security track: schedule the 45-min security ops call (Wed 10am PT confirmed) to walk the network diagram, confirm egress IPs, and agree a BYOK migration plan and audit export path.
3) If Security requires full-identifier processing inside Redwood, we will present a Private VPC option: expected lead time 4–6 weeks longer than Dedicated plus a Private deployment fee; we'll include this in the proposal.

Action items: 
- Rajiv / Security: share the sanitized asset list and any specific egress IP ranges pre-call (by Tue EOD).
- Ben / Karthik / Mina: prepare the ops checklist and an explicit cost delta for Private VPC vs Dedicated (I’ll include the storage-retention add-on estimate for the 7-year logs).
- Procurement: I’ll upload the draft SLA to HubSpot and start a DocuSign template for the pilot terms.

If that sounds right I’ll send the calendar invite for Wed 10am PT and include the prep checklist and links.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this to pilot.

Mina
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
